channel.title: Rushabh Shah · Blog
channel.description: Articles on DevOps, Kubernetes, Docker, and observability, by Rushabh Shah, Docker Captain and Grafana Champion.

item.title: CKA exam day: PSI bridge, terminal, kubectl aliases
item.description: The logistics nobody mentions until exam day: PSI Secure Browser setup, what the exam terminal actually gives you, kubectl aliases worth memorizing, and how to manage the clock.

item.title: Kubernetes v1.37 (Garhwal): 52 forts, 67 changes, and what actually breaks
item.description: A complete, plain-language guide to Kubernetes v1.37 Garhwal: every Stable graduation, the Beta features now on by default, working YAML for the ones you'll use, and the four changes that can stop your upgrade dead.

item.title: What the CKA actually tests in 2026
item.description: The CKA is a live-terminal, performance-based exam against real clusters, not multiple choice. Here's the format, what it actually covers, how to practice, and where people lose time.

item.title: Is KCNA worth $250 as a first certification
item.description: KCNA is multiple choice, has no prerequisite, and is the cheapest cert in the Linux Foundation catalog. Here's what it actually covers, and who should skip it entirely.

item.title: The Kubestronaut path and what it really costs
item.description: Kubestronaut means holding five CNCF certifications at once: KCNA, KCSA, CKA, CKAD, and CKS. Here's the real cost breakdown, a realistic study timeline, and who it's actually for.

item.title: My CNCF DevStats score is 178, and now I can't stop checking it
item.description: A tiny tool turns your GitHub username into a CNCF contribution score. Mine came back 178. Here's what that number is actually made of, and how to check yours.

item.title: CKA vs CKAD vs CKS: which to take first
item.description: CKA, CKAD, and CKS all share the same live-terminal format and the same $445 price tag, but they certify very different jobs. Here's who each one is for and what order makes sense.

item.title: Hello, world: the blog now lives on rushabhshah.dev
item.description: Why I moved my writing from Hashnode to my own domain, and how this markdown-powered blog with scheduled publishing works under the hood.
